title: The Float That Looked Short
story: Before the craft market opened, Elise counted the float and compared it with the notebook. The cash was lower than the written total by the price of two mugs. She found a Friday sale that had been entered twice, which made the book too high. She corrected the entry and wrote the true starting amount on a fresh page for Saturday.

vocabulary.definition: The starting cash a seller keeps in order to give change.
The full amount when numbers are added together.

quiz.question: By how much did the cash seem lower than the book?
options: By the price of two mugs
By the price of the notebook
By the whole of Friday’s market
By the cost of a fresh page
quiz.correctAnswer: By the price of two mugs
quiz.explanation: The cash was lower than the written total by the price of two mugs.
quiz.supportingSentence: The cash was lower than the written total by the price of two mugs.

quiz.question: What does the double entry explain?
options: The book was too high, while the cash was really there
Two mugs had been stolen before opening
Friday’s market had never taken place
The float had been spent on a new notebook
quiz.correctAnswer: The book was too high, while the cash was really there
quiz.explanation: A sale entered twice made the book too high, so the gap came from the record.
quiz.supportingSentence: She found a Friday sale that had been entered twice, which made the book too high.

quiz.question: Why is the fresh page useful for Saturday?
options: It starts the day from the corrected figure
It hides every Friday sale
It raises the price of the mugs
It takes the cash out of the tin
quiz.correctAnswer: It starts the day from the corrected figure
quiz.explanation: She wrote the true starting amount on a fresh page after correcting the mistake.
quiz.supportingSentence: She corrected the entry and wrote the true starting amount on a fresh page for Saturday.

quiz.question: What does float mean in this story?
options: Starting cash kept for giving change
A book of old sales
A mug sold on Friday
A page that has never been used
quiz.correctAnswer: Starting cash kept for giving change
quiz.explanation: Elise counts the float before opening, which is the cash the stall starts with.
quiz.supportingSentence: Before the craft market opened, Elise counted the float and compared it with the notebook.

quiz.question: Why did Elise correct the notebook entry?
options: So the written total would match the real cash
So Friday would disappear from the records
So the float would shrink by two more mugs
So Saturday could begin with no figure
quiz.correctAnswer: So the written total would match the real cash
quiz.explanation: She corrected the entry that had made the book too high, then wrote the true amount.
quiz.supportingSentence: She corrected the entry and wrote the true starting amount on a fresh page for Saturday.
